# pf_table (Resource)

The contents of a pf table that pfapid manages. The table itself is declared in the firewall's base ruleset (`table <name> persist`) and listed in the pfapid policy; this resource owns its entries.

Creating the resource replaces whatever the table held; destroying it empties the table. Changes use commit-confirm like `pf_anchor`. Entries added by hand (`pfctl -T add`) show as drift and are removed by the next apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Contents of <k8s_nodes>, declared in the base ruleset as
#   table <k8s_nodes> persist
resource "pf_table" "k8s_nodes" {
  name = "k8s_nodes"
  entries = [
    "10.70.1.10/32",
    "10.70.1.11/32",
    "10.70.1.12/32",
    "2001:db8:70::/64",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `entries` (Set of String) Canonical CIDR prefixes, IPv4 and IPv6 mixed (`192.0.2.10/32` for one host). May be empty.
- `name` (String) Table name, as in `<name>`.

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Version of the committed table contents.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pf_table.k8s_nodes k8s_nodes
```
